title: Common semantic errors in C++
recap: A semantic error is valid C++ that does the wrong thing: integer division, an off-by-one bound, an uninitialized value, or a condition using the wrong operator can all survive compilation.
Trace a concrete failing input through the program. Change one suspected cause at a time and rerun the failing test along with earlier passing cases.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice common semantic errors in c++.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement averageScore(total, count), returning a floating-point average. Return -1.0 if total < 0 or count <= 0. Inputs are at most 10000. In particular, 5 / 2 must produce 2.5 rather than 2.0. This challenge targets integer division, incorrect guards, and forgotten return paths.
hints: Convert an operand before division, not the truncated result afterward.
A total of zero is valid; only negative totals are invalid.
